response: {"hypotheses":[{"title":"Cross-module counterexample first","claim":"Appending exactly this one system-prompt instruction—\"Before broad verification of a multi-module Python change, identify the most plausible silent contract violation at a changed module boundary, run the cheapest check capable of falsifying that contract first, then use only the remaining pre-deadline verification budget on broader checks.\"—will, versus no appended instruction with all other conditions fixed, reduce regression_count without increasing deadline misses; pass_rate, tool_calls, wall_time, and cost will be measured to determine whether the tradeoff is favorable.","rationale":"The named causal mechanism is counterexample-guided verification: converting the patch into a concrete cross-module failure hypothesis focuses the earliest, cheapest check on a likely silent correctness defect, so an actionable failure can be found before expensive broad suites consume the deadline. A paired A/B test should use hidden multi-module tasks, randomized condition assignment, repeated seeds, identical time and tool budgets, and trace audits that score whether the predicted contract, falsifying check, and subsequent budget use were actually observable.","assumptions":["Patch context is sufficient for the agent to infer a plausible boundary contract and failure mode.","A cheap falsifying check can often distinguish contract preservation from violation.","Broad verification remains feasible within the residual budget when the targeted check passes quickly.","Held-out evaluation prevents direct knowledge of hidden regression cases."],"risks":["Anchoring on one plausible failure can divert effort from a different, less obvious regression.","The inferred contract may be wrong or incomplete, producing a passing but uninformative check.","Generating a custom falsification check may cost more time and tokens than running an existing targeted test.","A failed check may trigger debugging or repeated reruns that exhaust the deadline.","Prioritizing one boundary can neglect independent failures in other touched modules, packaging, configuration, or end-to-end flows.","The instruction may improve benchmark-specific reasoning traces without improving hidden-test correctness."]}]}
